en: The Essential Yoga Method of Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa Bodhisattva,
one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Now, following the Yoga system and the teachings of the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*,
I shall explain the method of wish-fulfilling recitation for the Maṇi-padma family;
by practicing this samādhi, one can become like Avalokiteśvara.
First, he selects his disciples— those of noble lineage who revere the Dharma,
who are honored and beloved by many, who possess wisdom and courageous diligence,
and whose resolve in *vīrya* never abandons awakened insight.
Exhaustively fulfilling filial piety toward one's parents, Possessing pure faith in the Triple Gem,
Joyfully practicing the bodhisattva path, With the four immeasurable minds uninterrupted for even a moment, And always delighting in the Mahāyāna Dharma.
Abiding in the bodhisattva precepts, Revering the ācārya and all noble beings,
A man of heroic valor who has accomplished steadfast power, Thoroughly proficient in the gateway of yoga.
Always delighting in the practice of tranquility, possessing wisdom and fearlessness,
one constantly adorns the body with ethical discipline. Diligently cultivating the Secret Vehicle,
one respectfully relies upon the path of the *naya*, remaining single-mindedly without any stinginess.
One who constantly delights in hearing the sublime Dharma,
Who has entered samaya and received empowerment from a master, And who, having been granted authorization,
will soon attain accomplishment— Such are the characteristics of this disciple.
Only then may the transmission be bestowed;
this is the wish-fulfilling jewel capable of accomplishing all activities.
As the sūtras describe, the locations are mountain ranges, flowing streams, and pure hermitages (araṇya).
In a mountain valley flowing according to one’s pleasure, free from all dangers and fears,
one should prepare offerings according to one's means. Facing west toward Maṇibhadra,
the King of Sovereignty, one should next pay homage to the Buddhas of the other directions.
Placing the five limbs upon the ground, prostrate with reverence as instructed;
having knelt for a long time with both knees on the ground, join the palms with an open heart and remain thus,
sincerely confessing all transgressions of the three karmas.
From past lives, I have wandered through birth and death;
now, before the Great Holy One, I repent with all my heart.
Just as the Buddhas of the past repented, so do I now.
May you grant the power of your blessings so that all sentient beings may be completely purified.
By virtue of this great aspiration, may both myself and others attain stainlessness.
The secret mantra is as follows:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’ham. Next, the practitioner should rejoice in the merit and wisdom accumulated by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The roots of goodness accumulated by the Buddhas of the past, present, and future,
as well as by the Bodhisattvas and all the noble ones— I join my palms and rejoice in them all,
just as I have rejoiced in the roots of goodness I myself have accumulated, with no difference in my joy.

Next, one should place the right knee on the ground, join the palms in the *padmaka* (lotus) gesture at the crown of the head, and visualize paying homage to the feet of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
The mantra is: Oṃ padmamahāviśuddhe.

Having paid homage to the Buddhas, one may sit according to one’s preference—either in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*), or the royal ease posture (*rājopaveśa*).
Having formed this mudrā of sitting, visualize Buddhas filling all of space,
each with their own body before you. Abiding within those assemblies of noble ones,
from above the knees, perform a whirling dance, joining [the hands] at the heart.
Like a lotus not yet in bloom, visualize and pay homage to all the Buddhas.
Next, bind the Samādhi-mudrā: firmly interlock the *tarjanī* and *madhyamā* fingers at the heart, and extend the *anāmikā* and *kaniṣṭhā* fingers. This is the Vajra-Padma-mudrā.
The Universal Holder of the Lotus, having already awakened the assembly of noble ones by forming this mudrā,
the Buddhas and the sons of the Sugatas who possess great renown,
embrace [the practitioner] through their wondrous discernment.
Recalling my original vow made before the All-Illuminating Honored One,
and because I have not transgressed his instructions, I shall now empower [this practice] to bring it to fulfillment.
Next, form the Samaya-mudrā of the Bliss, Delight, and Joy of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
The ten fingers are firmly bound; the thumbs and ring fingers are joined at their centers.
The thumbs and little fingers are each joined and held upright.
The secret mantra is as follows:
By displaying this mudrā, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas,
and Vajradharas are thoroughly and wondrously delighted.
Next, one should open the door of the heart and enter the vajra-jñāna syllable.
Contemplate the two breasts; on the right is *tra* and on the left is *ṭa*, like the panels of a palace door.
With the supreme vajra-bond, the three karmas arise simultaneously; striking the heart, the two syllables open.
The mantra says:
"The seeds perfumed since beginningless time, the afflictions thus accumulated—
now, by means of the mudrā for summoning transgressions, I gather them together to shatter them."
The ten fingers are firmly bound; the thumbs and ring fingers are extended like needles, while the index fingers are bent like hooks.
Visualizing the summoning of all sins, one contemplates the various forms of those transgressions—hair standing erect, naked, and black in form.
Reverse the seal and pierce the heart; having touched [it], recite the secret mantra because the three karmas are in accord.
By reciting this "summoning of all accumulated sins," once the summoning is complete, one may then perform the rite of destruction.
The mantra says:
Having summoned [the offender] into the palm, perform the rite of destruction;
with the hands joined within in the *pūrvamudrā*, recite "MĀṂ" to bind all sins.
Extending both hands straight with palms joined, one should visualize the syllable *ṭaḥ* as a vajra;
by clashing them together like crushing a mountain,
with wrathful words and a furious form, one can purify all evil realms.
Having recited [the mantra], one should clasp hands with the gesture of patience; seven times and three times as appropriate,
by means of this corresponding gate and through the skillful means of the former Buddhas,
the sins accumulated by the three karmas and immeasurable, most heavy obstacles [are purified].
Having performed this destruction, like fire consuming dry grass,
sentient beings are perpetually deluded and do not understand this principle; therefore,
out of the Tathāgata’s great compassion, he has opened this secret and wondrous gate.
Next, one should form the entry mudrā: with the two hands firmly bound as the Tathāgata-jñāna syllable,
insert the dhyāna and jñāna fingers into the center,
and join the vajra and effort fingers together like the shape of a ring.
Visualize a lotus with eight petals before you;
upon it is placed the letter A, adorned with two dots.
This wondrous syllable is called "Evil" (A), white in color like jade or snow, radiating forth a thousand rays of light.
Visualize the syllable with the power of progress; Place it within the heart to pacify the three karmas.
Simultaneously applying these functions, recite this secret mantra:
"Once visualized as having entered the heart, The form of the syllable becomes even more radiant."
The practitioner should contemplate this: because the fundamental nature of phenomena is unborn, one will before long realize tranquility.
All Tathāgatas of the three times, through their vajra body, speech, and mind, employ wondrous skillful means.
Holding the vajra-fist, close the gate of the heart with this;
by means of the syllable Jñāna (JÑĀ), one attains firmness.
Then, bend the forefinger and place it upon the back of the ring finger; having touched the chest with this mudrā—
The practitioner, abiding in meditative equipoise, firmly binds both hands and places them palms upward beneath the navel;
with the thumbs and index fingers in the shape of lotus petals, this is called the Samādhi-mudrā. Recite this secret mantra:
Exhaling and inhaling, dwelling in the mindfulness of *ānāpāna*, the Buddha pervades all of space. With a snap of the fingers, he awakens me:
"O Son of the Buddha, how will you achieve supreme, perfect enlightenment?"
Not knowing the sublime Dharma of the true nature of all Tathāgatas, the practitioner, having been awakened by what he had heard, spoke again, saying:
"What is called 'reality'? I pray that the Most Victorious Honored One will explain it."
All the Buddhas were filled with joy and uttered these supreme words:
"Excellent, O Mahāsattva! You have been able to ask such a question.
Contemplate within your mind the gateway of the syllable 'a' that resides therein."
With the syllables penetrating the mind, recite this secret mantra as follows:
one should silently recite it once, then visualize it as a lunar disc;
for the sake of further increasing one's diligence, recite these wondrous words again:
Within the mind-moon disk, made perfectly full and utterly pure,
one should visualize a wondrous lotus flower; upon it, place the precious vajra and the secret mantra, which says:
The volume of its circulation is like space, pervading the three realms.
Again, recite these wondrous words: "The vajra speech is free from sound;
herein one draws forth the wondrous lotus and emits thousands of blazing rays of light."
Within each and every ray of light, there are immeasurable Buddha-fields;
within those fields are wondrous lotuses. One should visualize holding a precious lotus—the Victorious Banner of the Precious Lotus—from which a sublime sound issues forth from the banner.
Whoever possesses meager merit, when dwelling in this samādhi of tranquility,
shall have all their aspirations fulfilled. Such bodhisattvas as these, for the benefit of all sentient beings, abide in meditative equipoise.
From within the lotus-womb, he wonderfully emits a thousand rays of light;
all are for the benefit of sentient beings. Through the perfection of generosity and the others, he universally enters all samādhis; this is the gateway of skillful means in the *naya*.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, you employ immeasurable skillful means,
manifesting in various emanation bodies; from birth through parinirvāṇa,
you turn the great, wondrous wheel of Dharma— all of which issues forth from the jewel of your mind.
The sublime Dharma that is taught is all accomplished by means of the wheel;
taking the wheel as sublime wisdom, one is able to sever all fetters and latent tendencies,
just like the turning of the Great Wheel of Dharma— this is the path of merit and wisdom.
Next, one should correctly observe and gradually withdraw the lotus of wisdom,
reciting the secret mantra:
"All Tathāgatas everywhere enter into a single essence."
Just as a bright mirror can manifest myriad images,
so too is the essential nature of the dharmadhātu. Abiding within the vajra-lotus,
it transforms into a precious lotus, becoming the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇi.
Visualize yourself as having a golden body with six arms,
holding a wish-fulfilling jewel; adorned with a crown of jewels upon a topknot,
you sit upon the King of Sovereigns (Īśvararāja) in the posture of preaching the Dharma.
First, the contemplation of the primary [truth], out of compassion for sentient beings;
second, the jewel of holding the mind, which can fulfill all aspirations;
third, holding the prayer beads, for the sake of delivering those in the animal realm from suffering.
With the left hand pressing upon Mount Jālandhara, he is accomplished and unshakable;
with the second hand holding a lotus, he is able to purify all that is contrary to the Dharma;
with the third hand holding a wheel, he is able to turn the unsurpassed Dharma.
With six arms and a vast body, he is able to traverse the six realms through the skillful means of great compassion;
observing the suffering of all sentient beings in this way, he sits within a lunar disc.
The body emits a thousand rays of light, And from the neck and back, a halo radiates all around.
Furthermore, visualize the moon disc at the heart, Upon which there is also a precious lotus flower.
By means of this, one becomes firm and steadfast; Contemplate one's own body as being immovable.
To abandon all delusive thoughts, recite this secret mantra:
"By the empowerment of this dharma, join the ten fingers like lotus petals;
extend the forefingers and bend them like jewels. Seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown."
Visualize the syllable *HŪṂ* at the heart, *TRAḤ* on the forehead,
*HRĪḤ* above the throat, and the syllable *AḤ* placed upon the crown;
by arranging the visualization in this manner, this body becomes like a vajra.
Furthermore, recite this secret mantra with the voice of a lotus-speech;
next, one should perform the consecration. The wise one joins the lotus-palms, with the index fingers shaped like jewels and the thumbs brought close together.
Place it upon the forehead and recite the secret mantra; visualize the Buddha conferring empowerment.
Then, using this sublime mudrā, separate the two hands on either side as if binding a lotus garland, and slowly lower them downward while releasing the fingers.
Visualize the gesture of hanging a white sash and recite these wondrous words:
Next, one should bind the armor. Forming the lotus-fist mudrā with both hands, circle them from the heart toward the back, and from the back, circle them toward the navel.
It moves toward the waist and both knees, then gradually ascends to encircle the back of the neck;
from the back of the neck it reaches the throat, then again encircles the back of the neck and returns to the forehead, finally encircling the back of the crown of the head.
Gradually disperse [the mudrā] from below the navel.
Reciting these secret words for the sake of gladdening all Buddhas, one should perform the Lotus-Pressing Mudrā:
with both hands forming the lotus-palms, press them skillfully to bring forth joy.
The mantra says:
Visualize before one's own body that the syllable-gateway *Hrīḥ* transforms into a lotus king, within which is the syllable *Hrīḥ*.
With *taraṃ* on both sides, the vajra, jewel,
and lotus transform together into the Honored One; holding exquisite jewels as before,
one visualizes oneself [as him], and what is visualized now is likewise so.
To ensure that their essence is non-dual, next perform the rite of invocation:
with the ten petals of the lotus not yet unfolded, and the thumbs and index fingers in the hook-gesture, recite this secret mantra; one should produce the sound of the lotus.
Once the practitioner has performed the invocation, they should next form the Lotus Rope Seal (*padma-pāśa-mudrā*).
Joining the lotus-palms as before, extend the two index fingers to touch like a ring;
this is called the Lotus Rope, which can fulfill all wishes and intentions.
One should recite this secret mantra to summon [the deity] into the wisdom-body;
once summoned into the wisdom-body, in order to prevent any movement,
one should further form the lotus-chain mudrā and maintain a resolute mind.
As before, join the palms in the lotus gesture; with the thumbs and ring fingers pressed together like rings, do the same for the index and little fingers.
Interlocking them like hooks and chains brings about sublime joy; this is the Lotus Bell Mudrā.
One should hold a lotus flower with the *citta* (wisdom) and *jñāna* (meditative concentration) mudrās inserted within it, stabilized by the *vīrya* (effort) mudrā like a ring.

Recite this secret mantra: OṂ JÑĀNA PADMAVIŚAYA HŪṂ. Next, one should recite the hundred-syllable mantra of the lotus, holding the *argha* vessel filled with fragrant water of saffron, white sandalwood, and camphor, and offer it as an oblation.
Next, one should perform both internal and external offerings. Regarding the offering to the Lotus King, the internal offering is as follows:
place the *abja* (lotus) palms at the heart with the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers extended straight; this is called the "Lotus Joy" (*padma-harṣa*).
Next, bind the flower-garland mudrā; with this, perform the offering.
Without altering the previous mudrā of joy, hold it forward with both hands while visualizing various precious garlands filling the entire realm of space.
The secret mantra is as follows:
Next, one should offer with the Gīta-mudrā to the Holder of the Wisdom Lotus;
furthermore, with the previously mentioned excellent mudrā, bend the palms so that they rest upon the fingers (the pāramitās).
From the navel gradually to the mouth, visualize it dispersing downward like the act of pouring;
then contemplate the sound of the kiṃnara. The mantra for making offerings to all the noble ones is as follows:

Next, one should form the Dance Mudrā: rotate the previous mudrā to the left and right, joining the hands in the wondrous *padmahasta* (lotus-hand) gesture; place it upon the crown of the head and scatter [flowers] from it.
Through these four offerings, one is able to attain great supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
The mantra says:
Having performed these four offerings, one can accomplish the most supreme matters;
next, perform the outer offering, presenting it with a joyful mind.
Directing the mind toward the boundless realm, the Dharma of offering incense with the lotus hand was spoken by all the Buddhas as a sincere word for the benefit of all sentient beings;
one should scatter [the incense] with the palm facing downward, like the motion of burning incense.
Recite this secret mantra and visualize clouds of incense offerings pervading the entire realm of space; having thus made offerings to the assembly of noble ones,
one should next form the flower mudrā with the thirty-two marks.
Adorning all Tathāgatas, one contemplates clouds of exquisite colored flowers and directs the mind to pervade all things. As before, joining the palms like a lotus,
one scatters them like a mass of flowers to make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
And all the sons of the Sugatas, imagine clouds of flowers filling the realm of space with exquisite fragrance; with the utmost majesty of the kalpa-trees,
recite these secret and wondrous words while applying the three karmas in unison.
Sentient beings are shrouded by ignorance, deprived of the light of wisdom;
for the sake of purifying them, one should form the Wisdom Lamp Mudrā:
with the previous lotus-palm gesture, the fingers of dhyāna and wisdom are held upright and pressed closely together.
Visualize a maṇi-lamp in the mind, emitting immeasurable light that illuminates the entire realm of space.
The wise one should then recite this secret mantra and subsequently form the mudrā of liberation for the unguent.
For the sake of purifying sentient beings, I offer this incense of ethical discipline (*śīla*).

With palms joined like lotuses, I scatter [the offering]; with the power of the ten perfections, I apply scented unguents at the heart, perfuming the habitual tendencies until the ocean of fragrance pervades all of space.
Having offered to the Buddha and those who are honored, and having performed the outer and inner offerings while reciting these secret words, one should then, in accordance with the sequence,
bind the fundamental secret mudrā facing the Lord of Secret Mantras.
First, recite the root mantra clearly seven times. Then, with palms leveled against the heart,
form the *mudrā* with the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers like lotus petals,
the *madhyamā* and *aṅguṣṭha* fingers in the shape of a *maṇi*, and all the remaining fingers like banners.
Recite the root mantra while contemplating the fulfillment of the wishes of sentient beings.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the heart-secret seal according to the previous root seal.
Bound by the precepts, the directions, and generosity, it is named the Fundamental Heart-Seal.
All various wishes and intentions, whatever the mind conceives through the application of this seal, shall all be fully accomplished.
The mantra is as follows.
Next, bind the随心印 (Anupūrvaka-mudrā): with both hands in a firm vajra-bind, form the maṇi-shape with the thumbs and index fingers, and extend the middle and ring fingers side by side.
The boundaries of the precepts are likewise expansive and straight; the acts of giving intersect and stand upright.
Next, visualize that from the mouth of the Honored One, secret words flow forth, clearly forming the path of syllables, radiant with light of five colors.
Interspersed with various excellent colors, they enter the opening of the *yugma* and are arranged within a moon disc at the heart; as brilliant as red lapis lazuli,
contemplate each one individually, following the sequence of the principle until awakening is attained.
Abiding in meditative concentration and practicing cultivation, one enters the gateway of the syllable A;
thus entering the visualization of the syllable Cakra (Wheel), one universally contemplates all syllables.
This is called the mindfulness of samādhi, through which one attains wisdom and liberation.
Through this union, one will before long attain omniscience.
If the sound is in accordance with mindfulness, one should abide in the visualization of the supreme, wondrous, and extraordinary deity; one must not harbor a restless or impatient mind.
Neither high nor low, neither lax nor hurried;
the wise one, free from discrimination and all deluded thoughts—
if one recites this one hundred thousand times, all that is sought shall be accomplished.
Holding a rosary in both hands— whether it be made of lotus seeds,
conch shells, other precious gems, or any flawless, radiant, and beautiful material—
one should string one hundred and eight beads, reciting [the mantra] seven times for each bead.
With the heart mantra and the heart-within-heart mantra, as well as the Vidyārājñī,
empower this ritual; having threaded the rosary beads,
pass each one through the center of the heart while chanting "svāhā" in unison.
Recite one thousand and one hundred and eight [times], according to one's capacity,
during four or three sessions. This rite was taught by the Buddha in the *Sādhanamālā* and the *Paramārthasaptati*, as well as in the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
If one practices in this manner, one realizes the first bhūmi in the present life;
beyond this, within sixteen births, one attains unsurpassed bodhi—how much more so the worldly siddhis?
What need is there to mention that which is not as desired in this life?
Having recited according to one's ability, again bind the samaya-mudrā and perform the eight offerings.
To dismiss the Lord of Secret Mantra, firmly bind the two hands:
the thumbs and ring fingers are in the shape of lotus petals.
From the heart to the face, they disperse; at the crown of the head, the palms join as flowers.
Visualize the Honored One in the midst of space, then return to the original palace via the same path.
The secret mantra is: [mantra].
Having dispatched the noble ones, one should abide in the visualization of one's own tutelary deity,
or in a secluded and tranquil place, recite the Mahāyāna *Laṅkāvatāra*,
the *Avataṃsaka*, the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and the *Tattvārtha*.
Having contemplated and practiced according to such scriptural teachings,
and having recited the sūtras, one should never interrupt the bodhicitta— whether walking, standing, sitting, or even while lying down to rest.
Siddhi shall be attained before long; this ritual procedure of Great Compassion taught by Vajragarbha requires no selection of lunar days,
constellations, times, food, or bathing— whether one is pure or impure.
One should always practice without interruption, remaining far removed from distraction and refraining from worldly affairs;
having completed the recitation, one should make aspirational vows,
bind the samaya mudrā, and pay homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

May I walk with ease; through this accumulation of meritorious deeds, by the power of my original vow for liberation, may I enable all sentient beings to swiftly attain all-encompassing wisdom. These four lines constitute the aspiration.
Composed as a Vajra Ritual Manual: For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, I now likewise compile this *Yoga-vidhi-essence* of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa.
